anti_overlap: Cost arithmetic, card-queue sizing, phase budgets, and gated-vs-streaming sequencing economics — another reviewer owns adjudication cost and scheduling.
Rater independence, pretraining correlation, chance-corrected agreement statistics, or whether agreement is valid evidence — another reviewer owns evidence structure.
Implementation mechanics: file formats, networkx usage, embedding model choice, script structure, or how adjudication cards render.
decision_lens: Ask of every relation the plan records: what performance would separate these two lenses, and does anything in the pipeline ever run it? A relation certified from definitions is a filing decision, not a discrimination. Grade evidence by whether it came from both lenses competing over one concrete situation. Where the plan's own data already shows confusion in use, treat that as the primary register and the generated graph as the derivative.
distance_rationale: An oral, pre-modern discipline whose entire pedagogy is discrimination between near-identical entities, and whose hardest cases share every constituent note. It developed an apparatus with no counterpart in engineering vocabulary — pakad, chalan, vadi/samvadi weighting, ascent-descent asymmetry, occasion-dependence — precisely because a scheme listing members provably fails to separate the confusable pairs. It also supplies a documented historical case of exactly the failure this plan risks: a complete, coherent, widely adopted classification that satisfied theorists and left practitioners with the same confusions it was built to resolve.
expected_isomorphisms: The thaat/mela filing scheme maps to the 4-type edge taxonomy and to open question 4; allied ragas sharing an identical scale map to the near-duplicate lens clusters and the 30 empirically confusable pairs; pakad and chalan map to the edge rationale as the load-bearing discriminating claim, with the type label as mere filing; vadi/samvadi weighting maps to which lens should dominate a given situation; ascent-descent asymmetry maps to directional confusability that a symmetric edge cannot express; occasion (samay) maps to the situation-dependence of whether a pair contrasts; the notated scale sheet versus the sung performance maps to definition-level model rating versus the situational-fit task that already failed, making the transfer bet inspectable; gharana variance maps to legitimate disagreement as eval material rather than adjudication load; establishing a raga by performing it maps to establishing an edge by surviving a generated item, inverting Phases C and F.
focus: Whether the plan's unit of record — a typed, symmetric, definition-level relation between two lenses — can carry the discrimination the eval is meant to measure, and whether anything in Phases A-F ever establishes a relation by putting both lenses in front of the same situation
name: fd-raga-allied-discrimination
persona: Apply the perspective of a musician trained in allied-raga discrimination — a tradition whose hardest pairs share every note and are told apart only by characteristic movement, weight, and direction, learned in performance. Its formal classification files ragas neatly and separates none of the confusable ones. A raga is not established by a scale sheet two theorists agree on; it is established by being sung, and corrected by an ear that has heard it go wrong.
review_areas: Notation vs performance: does any phase establish an edge by putting both lenses against one situation, or is Phase C only definition-level rating — the register that failed at situational fit?
The filing-scheme problem: do complements/contrasts/refines/sequences actually separate any pair the eval confuses, or do they sort lenses into bins while leaving the hard pairs inside the same bin?
Pakad: the rationale, not the type label, carries the discriminating claim. Is validation aimed at the label when the testable asset is 'name the situation where one fits and the other misleads'?
Direction: reaching for lens A when B fits is not the same error as its inverse. Do edges, validation, and item generation preserve direction, or is a symmetric relation doing a directional job?
Allied pairs the register omits: 26 of 30 empirically confusable pairs carry no edge. Is confusion-in-use ever promoted to primary evidence, or only demoted to a candidate feed in Phase D?
Occasion-dependence: the plan types a relation as a property of a pair, but two lenses may contrast only for some situations. Can lens_edges.json represent that at all, and what breaks if it cannot?
Variance as material: is a rater disagreement or an mk split treated as noise to adjudicate away, when a pair trained judgment genuinely splits on is the highest-value eval item the plan could ship?

severity_examples.condition: The eval measures the same belief that produced the graph, and the 26 empirically confusable pairs holding no edge stay invisible — the exact pathology the audit's ground-truth collision already demonstrated, now baked into v2 gold
severity_examples.scenario: Eval-v2 items are generated only from contrasts edges whose validation tested a definition-level relation, never a situation

severity_examples.condition: Phase F generates from an edge that cannot answer 'what would you see if one lens fits and the other does not', so the item's designated-correct answer has no defensible basis and the eval inherits an unfalsifiable claim
severity_examples.scenario: An edge is marked validated on the type label with no separating situation recorded

severity_examples.condition: Item construction cannot distinguish the common error (reaching for the familiar lens when the specific one fits) from its rare inverse, so distractor placement is arbitrary and item difficulty is uncontrolled
severity_examples.scenario: Confusability is stored and validated symmetrically

severity_examples.condition: Pairs that genuinely divide trained judgment — the most discriminating material available — are consumed as adjudication work and never survive as eval items or as recorded ambiguity
severity_examples.scenario: Rater disagreements and mk's 14 split pairs are routed only to resolution

source_domain: Hindustani raga practice — allied-raga (samaprakriti) discrimination, pakad and chalan as identity, thaat classification vs performed distinction
success_hints: Name the performance that would settle a claim: for any doubted edge, state the concrete situation where the two lenses visibly diverge, and whether the plan ever generates it.
Prefer a test that inverts the pipeline — generate situations first, observe which lenses compete over them — to another pass of rating edges that already exist.
Use the plan's own counts (414 contrasts, 30 confusable pairs, 26 with no edge, 14 split pairs) as the evidence any proposal must explain.
Trace one named case (the three trust lenses, or one of mk's split pairs) through Phases A-F and state what the pipeline concludes about it.
Distinguish 'the label is wrong' from 'the label cannot be right or wrong' — a relation with no separating situation is not yet a claim.
task_context: Stress the plan's central bets before mk ratifies it as a /goal: (1) that dual-rater edge validation will work where dual-rater item labeling already failed in this exact domain; (2) that graph-quality-first beats streaming/incremental restart of eval item generation; (3) that mk's adjudication attention is spent on the right units — edges vs node merges vs generated items; (4) that the 4-type edge taxonomy is the right substrate for a discrimination eval at all. Surface missed alternatives and any cheaper falsification tests that should run before the full overhaul. A wrong call wastes weeks of graph work and mk's labeling budget. The object of review is the proposed plan document: its Phases A-F, its Constraints and doctrine section, its drafted goal text, and its Known open questions.
